item.title: On digit-appending walks along linear recurrences
item.description: arXiv:2610.18919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study digit-appending walks in base $b\geq 2$ along integer linear recurrences with minimal characteristic polynomials having a unique simple dominant root $\alpha$ that lies outside the unit circle. We prove that if $\alpha$ and $b$ are multiplicatively independent, then no infinite walk can have uniformly bounded appended digit lengths. In contrast, we show that when the appended digit length can be unbounded, the same independence hypothesis implies the existence of infinite walks.
item.dc:creator: Arya Mosahab, Sahitya Boyyakar, Glenn Bruda, Scott Duke Kominers, Steven J. Miller

item.title: Large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials and trilinear sums over short intervals
item.description: arXiv:2610.18923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, Matom\"{a}ki, Pandey, Pliego, Ter\"{a}v\"{a}inen and Wang improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate of trilinear sums over short intervals of length $x^{\theta}$, which naturally reduces to estimating mean values of products of three Dirichlet polynomials. Based on recent works of Guth and Maynard and Chen, Gupta and Li on new large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, they improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for $\theta > \frac{3}{5}$. In this paper, we use their method to improve the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for $\frac{1}{2} < \theta < \frac{4}{7}$ and get new results for all $\frac{1}{2} < \theta < 1$. Our result yields improvements on many problems, including the work of Li on primes in short intervals of length $x^{0.52}$.
item.dc:creator: Runbo Li

item.title: Orthogonality relation between $GL(3)$ coefficients and additive characters with linear and non-linear phases
item.description: arXiv:2610.18928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the distribution and oscillatory properties of prime-supported Fourier coefficients attached to a Hecke--Maass form for $\mathrm{SL}(3, \mathbb{Z})$ twisted by additive characters. For linear phases involving irrationals of finite type, we construct an automorphic variant of Vaughan's identity and exploit bilinear cancellation to obtain an unconditional power-saving estimate. For non-linear phases $e(\alpha n^\theta)$ with $0 < \theta < 1$, we refine the Type~II bilinear forms via Weyl differencing and modern exponent pair methods. Combined with the analysis of untwisted $\mathrm{GL}(3)$ sums, this framework breaks the $2/3$-barrier of Jiang and L\"u and widens the admissible range of non-trivial cancellation.
item.dc:creator: K. Venkatasubbareddy

item.title: Some Bounds on the Lehmer Index
item.description: arXiv:2610.18943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, the relationship is studied between the Lehmer index and the reciprocal sum of the prime factors of a Lehmer number. Some upper bounds and a lower bound are proposed for the Lehmer index. Another constraint on Lehmer index is also proposed if a Lehmer number has 3 as its prime factor.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Zhuang

item.title: Elliptic curves attached to Jacobians with imaginary multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2610.19069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let M be an imaginary quadratic field and A be an abelian variety of odd dimension g defined over Q for which there is a unitary algebra embedding of M in End^0(A_M) of signature ((g+1)/2,(g-1)/2). Extending a result by Fit\'e and Goodman, we show the existence of an elliptic curve E over Q with complex multiplication by M such that H_et^1(E_Qbar, Q_l) is a G_Q-subrepresentation of H_et^g ( A_Qbar, Q_l((g-1)/2) ). The main results of the article consist on explicit descriptions of E for A in two different families. First, when A is the Jacobian of the curve y^2 = xh(x^2), where h in Z[x] is a degree g monic separable polynomial with nonzero h(0), we show that E is given by y^2 = x^3 + h(0)x. Second, when A is the Jacobian of y^3=f(x), where h in Z[x] is a degree 4 monic separable polynomial, we show that E is given by y^2 = x^3 + 16 disc(f). This latter result builds on work by Laga and Shnidman in the bielliptic case, of which we give an alternative proof by means of a new p-adic method. As an application, we derive a practical average polynomial time algorithm to compute the Zeta functions of the reductions of a Picard curve.
item.dc:creator: Francesc Fit\'e, Francesc Pedret

item.title: A new way integral for the $n$-fold cover of $SL_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.19110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\pi$ be a genuine irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of the $n$-fold cover $SL_2^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ of $SL_2(\mathbb{A})$, $n \geq 3$ odd, and let $\tau$ be the genuine representation of $GL_1^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ obtained from a unitary Hecke character of $\mathbb{A}^\times$. We prove that, for a certain choice of data, a new way integral for $SL_2^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ represents the partial $L$-function $L^S(ns+\tfrac12,\pi\times\tau)$. The integral is derived from the generalized doubling integral of Cai, Friedberg, Ginzburg and Kaplan, following the idea of Ginzburg and Soudry.
item.dc:creator: Tianxiang Liu

item.title: An algebro-geometric approach to profinite iterated monodromy groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.19117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We carefully construct the profinite iterated monodromy group of a rational map as a quotient of the \'etale fundamental group of the punctured projective line. In doing so, we prove a number of folklore results regarding profinite IMGs; in particular, their topological generation by inertia concentrated in the post-critical orbit, and their relationship with the discrete iterated monodromy group over $\mathbb{C}$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Tedeschi

item.title: A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.19193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an infinite family of solutions to the Mondrian art problem with absolute defect bounded above by $280$, of side lengths $n_0 = 315$, $n_1 = 106785$, and $n_{j+2} = 340n_{j+1} - n_j$, where $n_j$ is congruent to $315 \pmod{630}$. This absolute bound shows that the minimum defect does not necessarily increase with $n$, providing a counterexample to a conjecture which has been open since the problem's original proposal. Our design is derived from a well-known seven-rectangle dissection over the real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{19})$, with non-integer side lengths; we tailor the side lengths to be integers via an infinite Pell family. Using the same method, we devise a second family with defect $560$ that contains infinitely many side lengths which are divisible by any given positive integer, implying that for any $k$ there are infinitely many side lengths $n \equiv 0 \pmod{k}$ with defect bounded above by $560$. This constant bound offers a dramatic improvement on the previous quadratic bounds.
item.dc:creator: Cooper O'Kuhn, Freeman Slaughter

item.title: Reductions of Galois representations of slope $2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.19293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime $\ge 5$. We determine the semisimplifications of the mod $p$ reductions of irreducible two-dimensional crystalline representations of the Galois group of ${\mathbb Q}_p$ of slope $2$ and weights $k\ge3p+4$ with $k \not \equiv 6 \bmod (p-1)$. The proof relies on the compatibility between the $p$-adic and the mod $p$ Local Langlands Correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.
item.dc:creator: Eknath Ghate, Sudipta Majumder

item.title: Zero-cycles and Brauer groups on certain Enriques surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the Chow group of zero-cycles $\text{CH}_0(S)$ for certain Enriques quotients $S$ of the Kummer surface associated to the product of two geometrically non-isogenous elliptic curves $E_1$ and $E_2$. We show that over fields of characteristic different from $2$ or $3$, the degree-zero subgroup $A_0(S) \subset \text{CH}_0(S)$ is 16-torsion. Over p-adic fields, we compute the transcendental Brauer group $\text{Br}(S)/\text{Br}_1(S)$. Using the Brauer-Manin pairing, we construct examples of Enriques surfaces for which $A_0(S)$ attains nontrivial 2-torsion elements arising from push-forward from the abelian surface $E_1\times E_2$.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Jaklitsch

item.title: Ternary polynomial relations and periods of cusp forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.19309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bachmann and van Ittersum conjectured that every polynomial $f\in\mathbb{Q}[x,y,z]$ satisfying $$ f(x,y,z)=f(y,z,x),\qquad f(x,y,z)+f(-y,x-y,z)+f(y-x,-x,z)=0 $$ is a sum of polynomials in two variables. We prove this conjecture over every field of characteristic zero and determine all homogeneous solutions. Moreover, restriction to $z=0$ identifies the degree $n$ solution space with the space of binary period polynomials of degree $n$ normalized to vanish on both coordinate axes. The solution corresponding to such a polynomial $q$ is $$ f(x,y,z)=q(x,y)+q(y,z)+q(z,x). $$ There are no nonzero homogeneous solutions of odd degree. For even degrees $n$, the symmetric and alternating solution spaces are each isomorphic over $\mathbb{C}$ to the space of weight $n+2$ cusp forms on $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The proof connects the polynomial relations with the cohomology of arithmetic groups through the rational Tits building for $GL_3$. Cusp forms enter both the description of the solutions and the proof that there are no others. The main theorems and the essential argument are formalized unconditionally in Lean~4 by AxiomProver.
item.dc:creator: Vasily Ilin, Ken Ono

item.title: Shapes of tame abelian number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.19311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The shape of a number field $K$ of degree $n\geq2$ is the similarity class of the lattice obtained by projecting $\mathscr{O}_K$ orthogonally away from the rational line in Minkowski space. It defines a point in the space of shapes of rank-$(n-1)$ lattices, $\mathscr{S}_{n-1}:=\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{Z})\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{GO}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})$, where $\mathrm{GO}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})$ is the group of orthogonal similitudes. Let $G$ be a fixed nontrivial finite abelian group, and let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ vary over tamely ramified Galois extensions with Galois group isomorphic to $G$. We study the variation of the shapes of such number fields in $\mathscr S_{n-1}$, where $n=|G|$.
item.dc:creator: Anwesh Ray

item.title: A folklore conjecture on multiplicative exponential sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.19464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a folklore conjecture on exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients: if $f$ is multiplicative with $|f(n)|\le1$, $(a,q)=1$, $|\alpha-a/q|\le q^{-2}$ and $q\le N/(\log N)^2$, then \[ \sum_{n\le N}f(n)\operatorname{e}(n\alpha)\ll\frac N{\log N}+\frac N{\sqrt q}. \] Complete multiplicativity is not required. We also prove two related conjectured bounds: the refinement in which $q$ is replaced by $q(1+N|\alpha-a/q|)$, when this quantity is at most $N/(\log N)^2$, and the corresponding bound for the sum with logarithmic weights. Finally, we show that the bound can fail for multiplicative $f$ satisfying only $|f(p)|\le A$ at primes and $\sum_{n\le x}|f(n)|^2\le A^2x$, for every fixed $A>1$.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Robles

item.title: Arithmetic Visibility in Polygons: Curved Sight in the Art Gallery
item.description: arXiv:2610.19506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the classical art gallery problem, a guard sees a target when the segment joining them lies entirely within the polygon. We explore what changes when sight may bend along regular arcs on absolutely irreducible curves, but only those defined by primitive integer polynomials of total degree at most \(d\) and coefficient height at most \(H\). We call such curves admissible sight carriers. Arcs can dramatically improve sight. In a one-sided comb, no straight-line guard sees selected targets in two different teeth, yet a single central guard sees a chosen target in every tooth along parabolic carriers. Sight can also fail in two different ways. Geometrically, the polygon may block every sight arc of the allowed degree between two points. For instance, in an alternating comb, the number of guards needed for a row of targets spanning the comb grows linearly with the number of sides at each fixed degree, even for carriers with arbitrary real coefficients. Arithmetically, no admissible carrier may pass through the points at all. Even in the unit square, at fixed \(d\) and \(H\), the proportion of rational targets that must guard themselves tends to one as the height bound grows. An algebraic target may lie on no rational curve of degree at most \(d\), however large \(H\) is. Both failures can be overcome for finite target sets by allowing the degree and coefficient height to grow. We show that every finite set of algebraic targets in a rational polygon becomes visible from any rational interior guard, with explicit bounds. We also construct, for every \(d\), arbitrarily large Galois orbits in the unit square, all of projective height \(4^{d+1}\), whose points must each guard themselves at degree \(d\) for every \(H\). Yet at degree \(d+1\) and coefficient height one, a single guard sees the whole orbit along \(Z(Y-X^{d+1})\).
item.dc:creator: Malik Barrett

item.title: On a problem on partitions into distinct primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.19534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a positive integer $n$, we write $L(n)$ in place of the maximum number of distinct primes whose sum is $n$, assuming there is a way of writing $n$ as a sum of distinct primes, with $L(n) = 0$ otherwise. Again if $n$ admits a partition into distinct primes, then we let $K(n)$ denote the number of parts in the unique partition that has a largest product, with $K(n) = 0$ otherwise. In the latest editions of Guy's classic text on unsolved problems in number theory, the problem as to whether or not $L(n) - K(n)$ is unbounded was left open, and it appears that this has remained open. We solve this problem in the affirmative. Our proof relies, to a large extent, on a consequence of Vinogradov's theorem together with a 1948 result due to Sierpi\'nski on the existence of primes whose gaps to the immediately preceding and following primes both exceed any prescribed positive bound.
item.dc:creator: John M. Campbell

item.title: The Density and Quantitative Upper Bound of Integers Not Expressible as the Sum of a Prime and a Zumkeller Number
item.description: arXiv:2610.19574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Zumkeller number is a positive integer whose set of positive divisors can be partitioned into two disjoint subsets of equal sums. In this paper, we investigate the additive properties of these numbers in conjunction with prime numbers. Specifically, we study the natural density of the exceptional set \(\mathcal{E}\) consisting of all positive integers not expressible as the sum of a prime and a Zumkeller number. Let $\alpha(x) = \#\{n \le x : n \in \mathcal{E}\}$ denote its counting function. We establish a quantitative upper bound for $\alpha(x)$, demonstrating that $\alpha(x) \ll x(\log \log x)^{-A}$, where $A = \log_2\left(\frac{2\pi^2}{2\pi^2-3}\right) \approx 0.2378$, thereby proving that the natural density of this exceptional set is $0$.
item.dc:creator: Ting Hon Stanford Li

item.title: On the Erd\H{o}s--Odlyzko--S\'ark\"ozy conjecture for prime-power moduli
item.description: arXiv:2610.19597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Erd\H{o}s, Odlyzko and S\'ark\"ozy conjectured that every reduced residue class modulo $q$ contains a product of two primes not exceeding $q$. O. Klurman, A. P. Mangerel and J. Ter\"av\"ainen (2023) have shown that three primes suffice when $q$ is sufficiently smooth. We study the moduli $q=p^\gamma$ that are powers of a fixed prime $p$ and we show that the third prime can be taken subpolynomially small. For any $q_\bullet\le q$ for which $q_\bullet\ge\exp\bigl(C(\log q)^{2/3}(\log\log q)^{4/3}\bigr)$, we give an asymptotic formula for the weighted number of representations of each reduced class as a product of two primes not exceeding $q$ and a third not exceeding~$q_\bullet$. We also show that the conjecture holds for all but a proportion $\exp\bigl(-c(\log q)^{1/3}(\log\log q)^{-1/3}\bigr)$ of the reduced classes. Here $C$ and $c$ are positive constants that depend only on $p$. Both results are unconditional and they rely on a wide zero-free region with no exceptional zeros for the Dirichlet $L$-functions attached to characters modulo $p^\gamma$.We also present conditional versions of these results for arbitrary $q$ under a quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: William Banks, Igor E. Shparlinski

item.title: Divisibility Estimates for Gaussian Norms and Almost-Prime Orders of a CM Elliptic Curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.20010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E:y^2=x^3-x$. We prove that $\#E(\mathbf{F}_p)/8$ is squarefree and has at most two prime factors for $\gg X/(\log X)^2$ primes $p\le X$. The proof follows the Gaussian CM sieve framework of Iwaniec and Jim\'enez Urroz and incorporates the intersection terms identified by Xie. For a squarefree Gaussian ideal $\mathfrak{a}$, we separate its largest rational ideal factor and use the resulting divisibility of both integral coordinates to control the large-factor tail. This transfers an ideal Bombieri--Vinogradov estimate to rational norm divisibility at level $1/2$, with any fixed power of the divisor function as a weight. We prove the corresponding distribution estimate for the switched product sequence and apply the transfer to both sequences in Chen's weighted sieve. The primes counted may be restricted to $p\equiv5\pmod8$; their normalized orders are odd, squarefree, and supported on primes congruent to $1\pmod4$.
item.dc:creator: SeungJu Lee

item.title: Primes between 8th powers?
item.description: arXiv:2610.20058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: OpenAI (using a non-public "internal frontier model'') has recently (6 October 2026) made a number of remarkable claims, including some claims regarding the quasi-Riemann hypothesis (QRH). While there are good reasons to be cautious regarding these claims, one can nevertheless ask what (if true) their implications would be. While there is widespread agreement that any version of the QRH will provide various improved bounds on the location of the prime numbers, I feel that there is some value in making these improvements explicit. Specifically, if we assume validity of the claimed 7/8 version of the QRH then I shall demonstrate (for all $n\in \mathbb{Z^+}$): 1) the existence of primes between eighth powers, in the interval $(n^8,(n+1)^8)$; 2) the existence of primes in the shorter interval $(n^8,n^8+8n^7)$; 3) the existence of primes in the even shorter interval $(n^8,n^8+n^7).$ Similarly for reals greater than unity $x>1$ one can demonstrate: 4) the existence of primes in the Hoheisel-style interval $(x,x+x^{7/8})$. All of this is contingent on the validity of the claimed 7/8 version of the QRH.
item.dc:creator: Matt Visser (Victoria University of Wellington)

item.title: Conguences for Odd Unimodal Sequences and a Problem of Bringmann And Lovejoy
item.description: arXiv:2610.20135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give a family of the arithmetic progressions in which the numbers of odd unimodal and odd strongly unimodal sequences are divisible by 2 and by 4. In particular, we answer a question of Bringmann and Lovejoy on the existence of such arithmetic progressions for odd strongly unimodal sequences modulo 4.
item.dc:creator: Koustav Banerjee, Manosij Ghosh Dastidar

item.title: Integral Specializations of Polynomials: Hilbert Irreducibility, Coprimality, and Density
item.description: arXiv:2610.20165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hilbert specialization property of a field, whereby irreducibility of polynomials is preserved under specialization of some of the variables, admits an integral counterpart where specialization takes place inside a ring and irreducibility is required over the ring. It is known that the ring $\mathcal{O}_K$ of integers of any global field $K$ satisfies this integrally Hilbertian property. Using a different approach, we reprove this result and strengthen it by showing that the corresponding integral Hilbert subsets of $\mathcal{O}_K^k$ are not only Zariski-dense, as required by integral hilbertianity, but also of positive density. A central ingredient is a generalization to the ring $\mathcal{O}_K$ of the Ekedahl--Poonen formula originally proved for $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$. This formula, of independent interest, gives the density of tuples in $\mathcal{O}_K^k$ for which coprime polynomials in $k$ variables and with coefficients in ${\mathcal O}_K$ take coprime values. Our generalization requires estimates for the number of points of bounded height in an arithmetic progression. We obtain such estimates as our third main result, thereby contributing to the theory of heights.
item.dc:creator: Angelot Behajaina, Pierre D\`ebes, Martin Widmer

item.title: New bounds for $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ shifted convolution sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.20182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shifted convolution sums of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ type have been extensively studied in several important settings, while a number of natural cases remain open. In this paper, we first revisit the shifted convolution sums involving $\lambda_\pi(1,n)$ and the divisor function $d(n)$, improving the recent power saving of $1/42$ obtained by Blomer and Li to $1/22$. We also treat the corresponding sums involving $\lambda_\pi(1,n)$ and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$, settling a previously open case and obtaining a power saving of $1/22$. Here $\lambda_\pi(1,n)$ denotes the normalized Fourier coefficients of a Hecke--Maass cusp form $\pi$ on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{Z})$, and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$ denotes the number of representations of a positive integer $n$ by a positive definite integral binary quadratic form $\mathcal{Q}$. The proof combines two circle methods with a different organization of the major-arc analysis. A key point is that the nonzero Poisson frequencies are kept together in a single coefficient vector, rather than estimated separately, which allows them to be controlled by a finite matrix norm. The zero Poisson frequency is treated separately: its contribution is independent of the reduced residue class, and its arithmetic mean cancels the constant term in the complementary Jutila weight before absolute values are taken. We make this cancellation explicit, including the relevant normalization and local factors. The same mechanism extends to the binary quadratic-form setting, while the remaining Jutila contribution is handled by the available correlation estimates.
item.dc:creator: Guangwei Hu, Guangshi L\"{u}

item.title: Genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.20214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields of odd characteristic. We express each as a product of two quadratic $L$-functions and explicit local factors at primes dividing the conductor, with a possible shift of the variable in one of the two quadratic $L$-functions. This product formula yields meromorphic continuation and functional equations. In the real case, we evaluate special values in terms of continued fractions and derive formulas for the product of class numbers of two imaginary quadratic function fields. These formulas are function field analogues of the Kaneko-Mizuno-Zagier formula.
item.dc:creator: Jigu Kim, Yoshinori Mizuno

item.title: On the Hardy--Littlewood--Chowla conjecture
item.dc:creator: Guangshi L\"u, Zhiwei Wang, Jie Wu

item.title: An upper bound for valuations of elliptic nets at primes of bad reduction
item.description:
arXiv:2610.20273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E/K$ be an elliptic curve over a field defined by the short Weierstrass equation and let $\mathbf{P}=(P_1, P_2) \in E(K)^2\setminus \{(O, O), (\pm P, \pm P)\}$ be a pair of non-torsion points, where $O$ denotes the point at infinity. We give a uniform upper bound for the quantity $\min(
u(\Phi_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})), 2
u(\Psi_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})))$, where $
u$ is a normalised discrete valuation associated to primes where $E$ has bad reduction and $\Psi^2_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})$, $\Phi_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})$ are rational functions for describing $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points $[v_1]P_1+[v_2]P_2$ on $E$, higher--dimensional analogues of division polynomials $\psi^2_n, \phi_n$ known as net polynomials. They are also elliptic nets, which are $n$--dimensional arrays with values in $K$ satisfying the same nonlinear recurrence relation that division polynomials do as well. Hence, they are useful in studying counting problems on elliptic curves.
item.dc:creator: Hang Lok Edison Au-Yeung

item.title: Quantitative lower bound for Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers
item.description: arXiv:2610.20311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each positive integer $N$, let $p_i$ be the $i$-th prime for $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and set $$ \Phi_N=\left\{\prod_{i=1}^{N}p_i^{a_i}:a_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}\right\}. $$ Write $f(N)$ for the largest cardinality of a subset of $\Phi_N$ containing no two distinct legs of an integral right triangle. We prove $$ N^{N-1}(\log\log\log N)\ll f(N). $$
item.dc:creator: Rongzhong Xiao

item.title: S-squareful values of binary quadratic forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.20316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shute showed that the leading constant in the asymptotic formula for squareful values of the form $ax^2+by^2$ does not match with the conjecture established by Pieropan, Smeets, Tanimoto and V\'arilly-Alvarado. In this paper, $S$-squareful values of this form are considered for $S$ the set of primes that divide $a$ and $b$. We prove an asymptotic formula for these numbers and show that the leading constant of the asymptotic formula still does not match the conjecture. Furthermore, we consider the updated conjecture established by Chow, Loughran, Takloo-Bighash, and Tanimoto regarding the leading constant for Campana points in the given setting and show that this constant is consistent with our computed constant.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Sophie Pohl

item.title: GCD and ABC inequalities for abelian varieties over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.20379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove two height inequalities for rational points on abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0. The first is the GCD inequality, which shows that the height with respect to a closed subscheme of an abelian variety of codimension at least 2 is much smaller than the usual height function. This can be viewed as a compact and geometric analogue of a theorem of Levin. The second is a special case of the (geometric) abc conjecture proposed by Vojta, which compares the truncated counting function and the usual counting function. This is a compact analogue of a theorem of Guo, Nguyen, Sun and Wang, and also resolves a conjecture of Buium, which was only known for traceless abelian varieties or constant abelian varieties previously. The proofs of these inequalities follow a common three-step pattern: from microscopic local estimates to local estimates, and then to global estimates. Building on the canonical Xie-Yuan heights, we control discrete counting functions by continuous integrals of Betti forms. The main new tools are uniform Nevanlinna-type estimates for families of linear entire curves on abelian varieties; combined with covering arguments based on Besicovitch theory and averaging, these handle overlaps and gaps precisely.
item.dc:creator: Guoquan Gao

item.title: Universal norms of partially de Rham $B$-pairs and perfectness in Lubin--Tate Iwasawa theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.20445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the behaviour of partially de Rham Selmer groups of $B$-pairs along abelian $p$-adic Lie extensions. In the cyclotomic case we compare them with the universal norms studied by Berger. For analytic Lubin--Tate $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules we prove that the $\Psi=1$ eigenspace is coadmissible of the expected rank over the algebra of analytic distributions and establish a comparison result between its Lie-algebra coinvariants and the projective limit of the partially de Rham Selmer groups of the attached $B$-pair.
item.dc:creator: Marvin Schneider, Rustam Steingart

item.title: The large sieve inequality and additive decompositions of sums of squares
item.description: arXiv:2610.20554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on the large sieve, we prove a new sieve estimate for sets which are missing various residue classes modulo prime squares. For certain interesting residue class configurations, our bound is a significant improvement over the corresponding Johnsen-Selberg sieve inequality. Our application of this sieve estimate is motivated by Ostmann's problem. We study additive decompositions of sums of squares and show that any non-trivial sumset decomposition must consist of two sets of roughly equal size: If $A_1, A_2 \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $A_1 + A_2 = \{x^2 + y^2 : x, y \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ and $|A_1|, |A_2| \geq 2$, then $\sqrt{x}/(\log x)^{9/2} \ll |A_i \cap [1, x]| \ll \sqrt{x}(\log x)^4$ for $i \in \{1, 2\}$.
item.dc:creator: Christian Elsholtz, Julia Stadlmann

item.title: Arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of modular curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.20575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the full generating series arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of two modular curves, with arbitrarily singular coefficients. This is the case $\operatorname{GSpin}(2,2)$ in Kudla's program.
item.dc:creator: Ryan C. Chen, Baiqing Zhu

item.title: The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.20600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every number field of degree $n$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has a defining integral polynomial of degree $n$ whose coefficients are all $O_n(\sqrt D)$ in size, thus resolving a 1998 conjecture of Ruppert. Our proof compares ideal lattices with their trace duals, via which we handle all number fields with the exception of CM fields whose maximal totally real subfields have small discriminant. We then treat the remaining fields by averaging completed Epstein zeta functions over all possible ideal classes and archimedean scalings, for which we make critical use of Hecke's formula and the subconvexity theorem of Michel and~Venkatesh. Our proof does not use the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Manjul Bhargava, Sameera Vemulapalli

item.title: $\ell$-Independence, slopes, and weights of $\ell$-adic cohomology groups of rigid spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\ell$ and $p$ be distinct prime numbers, $K$ a local field with residue characteristic $p$, $C$ a complete algebraically closed extension of $K$, and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid space over $K$. When $\mathop{\mathrm{char}} K = 0$, we prove that the alternating sum of traces of elements in the positive part of the Weil group acting on $R\Gamma(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$ is independent of $\ell$ and is an integer, extending a result of Mieda to the singular case. We also give optimal bounds for the $p$-adic valuations of the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius liftings acting on $H^i(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$, proving a conjecture of Lu--Zheng. In the general case, we give optimal bounds for the $p$-adic valuations of the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius liftings acting on $H^i_c(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$, and we show that these eigenvalues are algebraic integers and Weil numbers, thereby extending results of Lu--Zheng and Mieda to the positive characteristic case.
item.dc:creator: Xiangdong Wu

item.title: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
item.description: arXiv:2610.19434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $\rho\colon G\to \GSp_{2n}(\Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ associated with $\rho$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $\rho$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by $\rho$. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\GSp_{2n}(\Q_p)$, under some assumptions, we prove the existence of certain paths in $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ and show that $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Aniruddha Sudarshan

item.title: Positivity and negativity for $h$-bases for $n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.19470v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A set $A$ of integers is an $h$-basis for $n$ if every integer in $[0,n] = \{0,1,2,\ldots,n\}$ belongs to the sumset $hA$, that is, can be represented as the sum of exactly $h$ not necessarily distinct elements of $A$. The classical postage stamp problem asks for the largest integer $n_h(k)$ such that $[0,n_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of nonnegative integers of size $k+1$. We consider the effect of allowing negative elements. Let $n^{\flat}_h(k)$ be the largest integer such that $[0,n^{\flat}_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of integers of size $k+1$ containing at least one negative integer. For $k=2$, we have $n^{\flat}_h(2) < n_h(2)$ if $h$ is odd or $h=4$ and $n^{\flat}_h(2) = n_h(2)$ if $h$ is even and $h \neq 4$. Proofs of these comparison results were autonomously discovered and formally verified in Lean by https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/}{Aristotle}, a formal reasoning agent developed by https://www.harmonic.fun/}{Harmonic}. In this paper we give new proofs of these results.
item.dc:creator: Wouter van Doorn, Pietro Monticone, Melvyn B. Nathanson

item.title: Proofs and disproofs of some conjectures on zero-sum problems of new types
item.description: arXiv:2610.19965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For integers $r\ge1$ and $n\ge2$, let $s_r(n)$ be the least $N$ such that every sequence of $N$ vectors in $\Z^r$, each nonzero modulo $n$, contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero modulo $n$ but nonzero modulo $n^2$. Let $w_r(n)$ be the corresponding least $N$ when any nonempty subsequence is allowed. These constants were introduced as zero-sum problems of new types by Z.-W. Sun. We prove $s_r(n)\ge(2^{r+1}-2)(n-1)+1$ by constructing an explicit sequence from a lattice polytope, \emph{disproving} his conjecture $s_2(n)=4n+1$ for $n\ge4$. We obtain $w_r(2)=2r+1$ by classifying all sequences avoiding such nonempty subsequences modulo $4$. We also \emph{prove} Sun's conjecture $w_2(n)=4n-3$ for $n=2^k3^\ell p$, where $p$ is a prime and $k,\ell\ge0$ are integers, by classifying the extremal sequences of length $4p-4$ modulo $p^2$ when $n=p$. For every fixed $n\ge2$, we prove $w_r(n)/s(\Z_n^r)=O_n(r^2/2^r)\to0$ as $r\to\infty$, where $s(\Z_n^r)$ is the classical Erd\H{o}s-Ginzburg-Ziv constant, with an explicit threshold on $r$ for strict inequality. Thus, for every fixed modulus $n\ge2$, Sun's proposed equality fails for sufficiently large $r$.
item.dc:creator: Yang Li, San Ling, Zhonghua Sun, Shixin Zhu

item.title: Reciprocal Dynamics in Congruence Jumping: Integral Orbits and Valuation Cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.20176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For fixed positive degrees $n,m$, alternating monic reciprocal transformations define a rational discrete dynamical system on the finite-dimensional coefficient space of polynomial pairs. This system arises from congruence jumping in polynomial divisibility problems, where a quotient move changes the polynomial state, but its coefficient dynamics can be studied independently. We prove that every state with nonzero constant terms returns after four alternating updates to its rational gauge classes and classify when this return orbit is realized over $\mathbb Z$. The local obstruction is encoded by endpoint $p$-adic valuation defects. After the first integral block, constant-term valuations evolve by an explicit matrix $M_{n,m}\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ whose trace depends only on $s=nm$. This yields a finite-order, elliptic-type regime for $s<4$, a parabolic dilation regime for $s=4$, and a hyperbolic regime for $s>4$. In the hyperbolic case, invariant thresholds, irrational eigencones, and discrete valley formulas give finite criteria for forward and bi-infinite integral orbits; nevertheless, failure can be delayed arbitrarily long. At the pointwise level, separated auxiliary-relation transport factors through the jumped-variable projection. One jump preserves the visible support rank, while two alternating jumps collapse it to dimension at most one; saturation cannot restore rank. In the quadratic specialization, a rank-two $p$-adic relation lattice gives an exact local cancellation-depth formula and a finite criterion on periodic Vieta orbits. We classify the fixed auxiliary relations that saturate indefinitely on an irreducible six-cycle and construct arbitrarily long persistence on parabolic and fixed hyperbolic orbits.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev, Dmitry I. Khomovsky

item.title: A prismatic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2610.20466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the category of constructible $p$-Kummer-\'{e}tale sheaves on the log adic generic fiber $(\mathrm{X},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{D}})_\eta$ for the stratification induced by a horizontal normal crossings divisor $\mathrm{D}$, showing that it is antiequivalent to a category of finitely generated unit Laurent crystals on the log prismatic site. We give a local description of finitely generated unit crystals on a framed log affine in terms of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules, and show pushforward compatibility for strict log smooth proper morphisms.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Pentland

item.title: Effective equidistribution of polynomial trajectories in $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)/\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a fixed matrix-polynomial trajectory in $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)/\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)$, we give a necessary and sufficient intrinsic Diophantine condition for its time averages to equidistribute at a power rate on its homogeneous orbit closure. The condition uses a lattice in the space of polynomial functions on the normalized orbit-closure group, each admitting a representative of total degree at most two in the matrix entries. These polynomial tests have a common degree bound of two, independent of the curve degree and optimal in general. The proof begins with a classification of the possible orbit-closure groups and derives lower bounds for polynomial coefficient vectors from the intrinsic condition. It combines quantitative nilmanifold equidistribution, unipotent tangent approximation, and effective flow estimates, with arithmetic separation and quantitative nondivergence controlling cusp excursions and periodic-orbit obstructions.
item.dc:creator: Hao Xing

item.title: Extensions of the Carlitz-McConnel and Blokhuis-Sziklai theorems for unions of cyclotomic classes
item.description: arXiv:2604.04126v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime, let $q=p^n$, and let $D\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^\ast$. A celebrated result of Carlitz and McConnel states that if $D$ is a proper subgroup of $\mathbb{F}_q^\ast$, and $f:\mathbb{F}_q\to\mathbb{F}_q$ is a function such that $(f(x)-f(y))/(x-y)\in D$ for all $x\neq y$, then $f$ must be of the form $f(x)=ax^{p^j}+b$. In this paper, we extend their result to the setting where $D$ is a union of cosets of a fixed subgroup of $\mathbb{F}_q^\ast$, under a mild assumption. In a similar spirit, we also investigate maximum cliques in related Cayley graphs over finite fields, strengthening several results of Blokhuis, Sziklai, and Asgarli and Yip.
item.dc:creator: Maosheng Xiong, Chi Hoi Yip

item.title: Root numbers for twisted Fermat quotient curves II
item.description:
arXiv:2604.20167v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is a sequel to the previous work of the author Yanagihara (2025). Let $\ell$ be an odd prime, let $N \geq 1$ be an integer, and let $\delta \geq 1$ be an $\ell^N$-th-power-free integer. Let $r,s,t>0$ be integers satisfying $r+s+t=\ell^N$. In Yanagihara (2025), the author computed the root number of the Fermat quotient curve $y^{\ell^N}=x^r(\delta-x)^s$ under the assumptions that $\ell
mid rst$ and that $\operatorname{ord}_{\ell}(\delta)=0$ or $\ell
mid \operatorname{ord}_{\ell}(\delta)$. In this paper, we study the case where the technical assumption $\ell
mid rst$ is dropped. As one such case, we compute the root number when $\ell^{N-1}\| r$ and $\ell
mid st\delta$.
item.dc:creator: Ryosuke Yanagihara

item.title: Potential semistability of Finite height Galois representations: Relative case
item.description: arXiv:2606.26043v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a $p$-adic field. We define the notion of finite height for an \'etale $\mathbb{Z}_p$-local system on a smooth affinoid adic space $\mathcal{X}$ over $K$ with semistable reduction. Using analytic prismatic $F$-crystals and purity results of Du-Liu-Moon-Shimizu (arXiv:2404.19603), we prove that if an \'etale $\mathbb{Z}_p$-local system over $\mathcal{X}$ is of finite height then its pullback along a finite \'etale cover of $\mathcal{X}$ is semistable. This answers a question of Tong Liu in the relative setting.
item.dc:creator: Kaustabh Mondal

item.title: Pythagorean triples in level sets of completely multiplicative functions
item.description: arXiv:2607.04903v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that given completely multiplicative functions $f_1,\dots,f_d$ taking values in the unit circle, there exist Pythagorean triples (i.e., integer solutions to $x^2+y^2=z^2$) with $f_i(x),f_i(y),f_i(z)$ all arbitrarily close to $1$ for all $i$. This is a new special case of the conjecture that any finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ has a monochromatic Pythagorean triple. Our proof combines vanishing averages for aperiodic functions with concentration estimates for pretentious functions. A similar proof is applied to obtain the analogous statement for more general equations of the form $ax^2+by^2=cz^2$ whenever $a,b,c$ are perfect squares satisfying the Rado's condition.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme Azevedo, Joel Moreira

item.title: Kronecker sequences beyond the torus: nearest-neighbour distances and best returns
item.description: arXiv:2609.13027v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study nearest-neighbour distances and strict best returns of cyclic orbits on $(V\times G)/\Lambda$, where $V$ is a finite-dimensional real normed space, $G$ has a bi-invariant ultrametric, and $\Lambda$ is an arbitrary closed subgroup. For the quotient of the maximum product metric, the number of distinct nearest-neighbour distances in every finite orbit segment is at most $P(\overline V)+1$, where $P$ is an open-ball packing constant and $\overline V$ is obtained by factoring out the continuous real part of $\Lambda$. For inner-product norms the bound depends only on the span of the projected subgroup. This gives $2^d+1$ for the maximum norm on $\mathbb R^d$ and strong-kissing-number bounds for inner-product norms, extending the corresponding real and adelic distance bounds. Our second main result is an exact abelianization principle: every such cyclic orbit is isometric, with its integer indexing preserved, to a cyclic orbit on an abelian mixed quotient $(V\times U)/\Lambda_{\mathrm{ab}}$. The construction preserves the reduced and effective real factors. Thus noncommutativity and non-normality enlarge the class of ambient presentations but not the class of cyclic-orbit metrics. The record-count identity and its growth consequences require only an isometric embedding of a metric space. For mixed homogeneous spaces we prove packing recurrences and, using abelianization, the sharp three-step and five-step recurrences in effective Euclidean dimensions one and two, without a normalizer assumption. We also extend the purely real recurrence to noncompact quotients and give counterexamples showing why the stronger real recurrence can fail after an ultrametric factor is added.
item.dc:creator: Evgeniy Zorin

item.title: Exact Moments and CM Periods of Reciprocal Quadratic Mellin Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2609.20201v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study exact moments and algebraic sampling of a reciprocal quadratic Mellin integral. A finite elementary formula determines every nonzero rational-weight first moment with specified branches. For $|b|<2\sqrt{c}$, mixed half-weight moments admit a dilogarithmic formula, and all even half-weight moments follow from one polynomial recurrence with a geometric error bound. At zero Mellin weight with $b=0$, half-integer deformations form an explicit two-function elliptic space. At the singular boundary, a two-parameter reflection gives a radical integral equal to $\pi$ for every parameter, a cubic logarithmic integral in dilogarithms, and an elementary golden-ratio specialization. All odd zero-weight boundary moments also have explicit formulas. For a reduced rational weight $p/q$, the sampling function generates a field of degree $q^2$ and genus $(q-1)(q-2)/2$, outside the stated degeneracies. Explicit cubic maps and a Picard--Fuchs certificate fix its elliptic period normalization and yield CM companion series with polynomial-weight closure. At denominator four, we determine the three elliptic quotient maps and their differential pullbacks. For the original kernel $(c,b)=(5,-2)$, the Jacobian is isogenous to $E_{1728}\times E_0^2$, and homological transfer gives gamma-valued periods of the sampling differential. Classical identities are credited and used as ingredients in these family-specific formulas.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: The Odlyzko-Poonen Conjecture on Irreducibility of Random Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.26771v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Odlyzko-Poonen conjecture states that a monic polynomial of constant coefficient $1$ and with remaining coefficients chosen independently and uniformly from $\{0,1 \}$ is irreducible over the rational numbers with probability tending to one as the degree tends to infinity. We prove the Odlyzko-Poonen conjecture unconditionally.
item.dc:creator: Constantin Kogler

item.title: On the Ordering and Injectivity of Lagrange Constants Associated with Certain Substitutions
item.description: arXiv:2609.32450v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the modern characterization of the Markoff spectrum via mechanical words and the Markoff Uniqueness Conjecture, we study the Lagrange constants of continued fractions generated by a parameterized family of substitutions $\phi_{a,b}$ defined by $0 \mapsto aa$ and $1 \mapsto bb$ with $b = a + 1$. Based on a three-fold arithmetic classification of pairs of rational numbers $0 \le x < y \le 1$, we investigate the order relations between the corresponding Lagrange constants $\mathcal{L}([\phi_{a,a+1}(G(x))])$ associated with the mechanical words $G(x)$. While an inequality is established for pairs of the second type (type (2)) whenever $a \ge 1$, the comparisons for type (1) and type (3) pairs hold for $a \ge 2$. Consequently, for any integer $a \ge 2$, where the order relations across all three types are completely determined, we establish an analogue of the Markoff Uniqueness Conjecture: the map $x \mapsto \mathcal{L}([\phi_{a,a+1}(G(x))])$ is injective on $\mathbb{Q} \cap [0, 1]$. Furthermore, supported by extensive numerical computations, we propose a general conjecture on the order relations for arbitrary $b > a$, highlighting a sharp phase transition in ordering behavior at the boundary $b = a^2 + 2$.
item.dc:creator: Shin-ichi Yasutomi

item.title: On the prime geodesic theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.01998v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We improve the error term in the prime geodesic theorem for the modular group. More generally, our result applies to any congruence subgroup of any indefinite quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Acosta Reche

item.title: The quality plane of $abc$-triples and the decomposition into gains
item.description: arXiv:2610.03212v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To a coprime triple $a+b=c$ we attach two coordinates, the quality $X$ and the logarithmic mass $Y$, whose ratio $\lambda$ measures the balance of the triple and lies asymptotically between $2$ and $3$. In these coordinates the $abc$ conjecture and Szpiro's conjecture for Frey curves become asymptotic bounds with thresholds $X=1$ and $Y=3$, and the direct implications between them follow from the range of $\lambda$. We then place the approximation and power gains of M\"uller, Taktikos and de Weger in the same plane. Relative to a chosen presentation of the triple, one exponent factor $f$ relates the gains to the coordinates, and Szpiro's conjecture for this family is equivalent to the asymptotic bound $f\le 3$ uniformly over all presentations. Under the two separate asymptotic gain bounds for a fixed choice of presentations, we obtain $\limsup X\le 9/2$ and $\limsup Y\le 27/2$ as the radical tends to infinity. Stronger conclusions depend on the presentation or on a joint bound for the gains. We close with numerical data and two research objectives.
item.dc:creator: R. Laniewski, K. M\"uller

item.title: The Artin-Davenport conjecture on cubic forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.08226v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that any integral cubic form in ten or more variables has a nontrivial integer zero. Like earlier authors on this topic, we use geometric methods to produce a zero in some cases, and the circle method in all other cases. New ingredients are required on both fronts: in the first case, bounds on the dimension of singular loci and incidence varieties, and in the second case, a stratified geometric sieve, together with stratification results for point counts over finite fields and a cube-root Hensel lifting analysis.
item.dc:creator: Dante Bonolis, Tim Browning, Jakob Glas, Victor Y. Wang

item.title: Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers
item.description: arXiv:2610.11965v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p_i$ be the $i$th prime, and let $f(N)$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of \[ \left\{\prod_{i=1}^N p_i^{a_i}:0\le a_i<N,\ a_i\in\mathbb{Z}\right\} \] containing no two distinct legs of an integer right triangle. We prove \[ f(N) \ll N^N (\log\log N)^{-1/1296}. \]
item.dc:creator: Rongzhong Xiao

item.title: Counting Rational Points on a Certain Bihomogeneous Threefold
item.description: arXiv:2610.15315v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $V\subset\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$ be the threefold $x_0y_0^2+x_1y_1^2+x_2y_2^2=0$, and let $U$ be the complement of its coordinate hyperplane sections. For the anticanonical height $H([\mathbf x],[\mathbf y])=|\mathbf x|^2|\mathbf y|$, evaluated on primitive integral representatives, we prove \[ N_U(B)=\frac{12\pi-14}{\zeta(2)\zeta(3)}B\log B+o(B\log B). \] The two projections combine lattice counting with uniform conic estimates. The main arithmetic step is an average of the fiber singular series, whose two main terms are related by Hilbert reciprocity. A moment estimate controls the full bad-prime part, and shape estimates permit the errors to be summed over the height region. We also check the leading constant with Peyre's constant.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Zhao

item.title: Some applications of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis to class groups and small generators of number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.18491v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an effective version of the Chebotarev density theorem, conditional on the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta function. Drawing on recent breakthroughs of OpenAI and Cureton--Thorner, we make unconditional the Ellenberg--Venkatesh bounds on $\ell$-torsion in class groups of number fields and extend an averaged result of Lemke Oliver--Smith to arbitrary families of degree-$d$-fields. Further applications are given to the least prime splitting and to small generators in number fields.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Frei, Efthymios Sofos, Martin Widmer

item.title: $2$-large sets are sets of Bohr recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2512.01997v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d$ be real numbers, fix $\delta>0$, and let $S$ be the set of positive integers $s$ such that $\|\alpha_i s\|_{\R/\Z}>\delta$ for some $1\le i\le d$. We prove that $S$ is not \enquote{$2$-large}, i.e. there is a $2$-coloring of $\N$ that avoids arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common differences in $S$. The case $d=1$ was previously known; here we prove the result in every finite dimension.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss

item.title: Classifying integer tilings and hypertilings
item.description: arXiv:2601.21445v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: There are two objectives to this work: to classify all tame integer tilings and to classify all tame integer hypertilings. Motivation for the first objective comes from Conway and Coxeter's modelling of positive integer friezes using triangulated polygons, which has received significant attention since the discovery of cluster algebras by Fomin and Zelevinsky in 2002. Assem, Reutenauer, and Smith introduced $\text{SL}_2$-tilings as generalisations of friezes, and Bessenrodt, Holm, and J{\o}rgensen classified positive integer $\text{SL}_2$-tilings using infinite triangulated polygons. Here we consider $N$-tilings, of which $\text{SL}_2$-tilings are the case $N=1$. We provide a geometric model for all tame integer $N$-tilings using a generalisation of the Farey graph in the hyperbolic plane. Highlights of this model include classifications of all positive integer $N$-tilings and of all positive rational friezes, with entries encoded by lambda lengths or weight data of triangulated polygons. The second objective is motivated by Bhargava's celebrated study of binary quadratic forms using integer cubes and by an observation of Demonet et al. that there is essentially only one three-dimensional positive integer tiling with $\text{SL}_2$ cross sections. We consider a richer class of three-dimensional tilings, which we call hypertilings, using the Cayley hyperdeterminant. We classify all tame integer hypertilings using generalised Farey graphs; remarkably, those with Cayley hyperdeterminant 1 prove to have a simple description in terms of triple Hadamard products of integer pairs.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Karpenkov, Ian Short, Matty van Son, Andrei Zabolotskii

item.title: Arithmetic hypergeometric $\mathcal {D}$-modules and exponential sums on reductive groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.00470v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a finite family of representations of a reductive group, we define a Laurent polynomial on the group. The exponential sum associated this Laurent polynomial is called a hypergeometric exponential sum. We introduce an arithmetic hypergeometric $\mathcal D$-module to study the hypergeometric exponential sum. It is an overholonomic arithmetic $\mathcal D$-module with a Frobenius structure so that the trace of the Frobenius at a rational point is the exponential sum. We prove that over the locus where the Laurent polynomial is nondegenerate, the arithmetic hypergeometric $\mathcal {D}$-module defines an $F$-isocrystal overconvergent along the degenerate locus. As an application, we get an estimation of the hypergeometric exponential sum.
item.dc:creator: Lei Fu, Xuanyou Li, Chenhan Liu

item.title: Generic Hodge and special Hodge--Witt polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.05892v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the Hodge polygon of the generic fiber of a proper smooth $p$-adic formal scheme over $\mathcal O_C$ lies on or above the generalized Hodge--Witt polygon of its special fiber.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yang
